newsitem.title: USA: San Diego landfill sale 'very positive' - Moody's.
newsitem.headline: San Diego landfill sale 'very positive' - Moody's.

text.p: An ambitious plan by San Diego County to sell its solid waste system for $184 million could boost the county's credit standing, Moody's Investors Service Inc said on Wednesday.

"The fact that they've found a buyer is very positive," said Moody's vice president and senior credit officer Nikolai Sklaroff. "Before we can reach any conclusions about this deal we need to know the details and how the county plans to use the proceeds from the sale."
San Diego County's chief administrator recommended on Wednesday that the county sell its solid waste system to Allied Waste Industries Inc for $184 million.
The county Board of Supervisors is scheduled to vote on the contract on August 12. Once approved by the board, the sale should close in November.
County officials said they plan to use the money to establish an environmental trust fund for the maintenance of inactive landfills and to build up the county budget reserve.

"The key question from a credit perspective is what does the board (of supervisors) do with the proceeds of the sale and whether it (the money) is used to improve the credit of the county by increasing the reserves and paying down debt," Sklaroff said.
Citing financial problems at San Diego County's solid waste system, Moody's last October lowered the county's long-term ratings to Baa1 from single-A.
